answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It survives because finality only counts for established attestators, so a fresh cluster cannot push transactions until it proves honesty across many epochs. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a nadir as the anchor of the cost. A mirror stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a garden holds...
